newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Foreigners snap up Singapore property in 2nd qtr.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners snap up Singapore property in 2nd qtr.

text.p: Foreigners bought 12.4 percent or 301 units of new private homes in Singapore in the second quarter of 1996, the Urban Redevelopment Board (URA) said on Friday.
The URA, which was releasing statistics on nationality of buyers of new homes for the first time, said a total of 2,432 new homes were sold during the quarter.
Of the total stock of private homes in Singapore, 8.9 percent or 12,633 units were owned by foreigners.
The URA also said the number of new homes under construction increased by 4.1 percent to 39,348 units at the end of the second quarter.
The number of uncompleted homes with sale licences increased by 7.8 percent to 29,609 units during the same period. Of these, 25.4 percent remain unsold at the end of the quarter.
Units unsold increase 13.1 percent from the 6,634 unsold units at the end of the first quarter.
The occupany rate of private homes during the period was 93.8 percent, up 0.5 percentage point over the previous quarter.
